topic: EMD exemption: when MSEs and startups don't pay bid security
draft:
Before you arrange an EMD, read one clause twice: the exemption clause.

Under Rule 170 of GFR 2017, bid security (EMD) is ordinarily 2% to 5% of the estimated value, and micro and small enterprises are exempt from it. In November 2020 the Department of Expenditure went further and told central ministries to ask for a Bid Security Declaration instead of bid security. Some buyers still ask for an EMD, so the tender itself decides what applies to you.

On GeM bids, the exemption comes with conditions. Bid documents we have read say:
1. Only manufacturers of the goods, or providers of the service, qualify under MSE. Traders do not.
2. You must upload the document for your category (Udyam for MSEs, DPIIT recognition for startups) with the bid.
3. State government buyers may still ask MSEs for an EMD if their additional terms say so.

So the check before every bid is three questions: is there an EMD or a declaration, am I in an exempt category for this item, and which page asks for the proof?

TenderTez lists the EMD clause and the exemption conditions from a tender PDF with the page they are on, so you can check them yourself: https://tendertez.in?utm_source=linkedin.emd_exemption&utm_campaign=emd_exemption

Sources: Department of Expenditure OM on bid security (12 Nov 2020); GFR 2017 Rule 170; a GeM bid document (RRI, GeM-Bidding-5263261).

On GeM, claiming the MSE EMD exemption usually means uploading the proof for your category with the bid: Udyam for MSEs, DPIIT recognition for startups. Check what the bid document asks for before the last day.

A turnover clause has four parts, and bids fail on each of them:

1. Which financial years: the last three, or three of the last five?
2. Average or every year: an average lets one weak year pass; "each year" does not.
3. Whole company or the tendered item: some tenders ask for turnover of the subject item only.
4. Proof: audited statements, a CA certificate in a set format, or both.

Then check the corrigenda. Turnover thresholds are one of the things corrigenda change.

TenderTez lists the eligibility conditions of a tender PDF with the page each one is on, and checks them against your company profile: https://tendertez.in/?utm_source=linkedin.turnover_clause&utm_campaign=turnover_clause

topic: Bid Security Declaration instead of EMD
draft:
Many central tenders now ask for a Bid Security Declaration instead of an EMD.

In November 2020 the Department of Expenditure told ministries that bid documents should carry a Bid Security Declaration provision instead of bid security. The same memorandum notes that some ministries were still taking EMD.

What a declaration means for you: no money is blocked, but if you withdraw your bid during its validity or refuse the contract, you can be barred from that buyer's tenders for a period stated in the tender.

So read two lines in every tender: does it ask for EMD or a declaration, and what is the penalty period?

Source: Department of Expenditure office memorandum on bid security, 12 Nov 2020.

draft: "Similar work" is defined in the tender, not by you. Read the definition: type of work, minimum value per order, client type (govt/PSU), and the period. Then match each past order to it before you bid.

Make in India preference in central procurement: Class-I local supplier has 50% or more local content, Class-II more than 20% and less than 50%. Below 20% is non-local. Check which class the tender accepts.

If you are a registered MSE, read the purchase preference clause in central tenders.

Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, an MSE that quotes within L1+15% can be allowed to match the L1 price and supply part of the tender. The policy also sets an annual target for central ministries and CPSEs to buy from MSEs.

Three things to check in the tender:
1. Does the clause apply to this item (works contracts are outside the policy)?
2. Are you a manufacturer or service provider for it (traders are excluded)?
3. What proof must be uploaded, and on which page is that asked?

Source: Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order, 2012 (as amended), summary on Vikaspedia.

Under GFR 2017 Rule 170, bid security normally stays valid for 45 days beyond the bid validity period. If a buyer extends bid validity, check whether your EMD or bank guarantee needs extending too.

Startups recognised by DPIIT can be exempt from bid security (EMD) in central procurement: a 2017 amendment to GFR Rule 170 exempts MSEs and recognised startups.

On GeM, bid documents ask you to upload the DPIIT recognition certificate with the bid to claim it. State government buyers may still have their own terms.
